trial_court: Court of Principal District Judge, Krishna at Machilipatnam (D.O.P.No.84 of 2020)
case_name: Viswanathapalle Tanuja Lanka Tanuja vs Nil
facts_of_case: Both petitioners are wife and husband who filed O.P. under Section 10-A of the Indian Divorce Act,1869 seeking divorce by mutual consent. They also filed I.A.No.304 of 2020 to waive off statutory period of six months.

legal_principles.principle: Where the Court dealing with a matter is satisfied that a case is made out to waive the statutory period, it can do so after considering certain guidelines.
legal_principles.held: Applying the above to the present situation, we are of the view that where the Court dealing with a matter is satisfied that a case is made out to waive the statutory period under Section 13-B, it can do so after considering the following:
cited_cases: Amardeep Singh Vs. Harveen Kaur, (2017) (8) SCC 746
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — in situations where parties have genuinely settled their differences

legal_principles.principle: The waiver application can be filed one week after the first motion giving reasons for the prayer for waiver.
legal_principles.held: The waiver application can be filed one week after the first motion giving reasons for the prayer for waiver.
legal_principles.significance: MEDIUM — in situations where parties have genuine reasons to waive the statutory period

outcome.final_order: Court waived off statutory period of six months for granting divorce by way of mutual consent.
